verdict_reasoning: Level 1b is where a committer would likely stop. already-exists-1: message #1 shows the WHERE form already gets the semi join, and the thread names no workload that emits the ON form and cannot change it. demand-1: 0002 rests on one Cloudberry discussion, and message #30 measures a query going from about 0.2 ms to 36 ms. Both are requests for evidence, and reviewers report 0001 correct. Confidence is low because the verdict rests on missing demand evidence and only 3 of 30 messages are visible.

brief.title: Pull up EXISTS sublinks whose join ON clauses reference the outer query
brief.problem: The planner turns `exists (select ... from tb, tc where ta.id = tb.id)` into a semi join, but keeps a SubPlan when the same correlation is written as `tb join tc on ta.id = tb.id`. Users who write correlated conditions in ON clauses get a per-row SubPlan and lose join reordering and index use.
brief.proposed_design: The 0001 patch takes the jointree out of the sub-select, checks that nothing else refers to the parent, then walks the jointree with a nullable-side flag. Correlated quals in ON clauses of inner joins not under an outer join's nullable side move to WHERE, and the sublink becomes a semi or anti join. The 0002 patch handles EXISTS in an outer join's ON clause referencing both inputs, using a LEFT JOIN against distinct correlation keys plus a CASE check.
user_visible_surface: Planner change: more EXISTS and NOT EXISTS sublinks become semi or anti joins, so plans change.
v5 touched guc_tables.c and postgresql.conf.sample, so it added a GUC; the thread never names it or says if later versions keep it.
author_claims: After the patch, ON-clause correlation gives the same plan as WHERE-clause correlation.
SQLsmith and a one-hour SQLancer run found no new errors with v10 and v11.
v8 fixes wrong results with outer joins found in v7 and leaves join.out unchanged.
0002 follows a Cloudberry bug discussion about EXISTS in outer join ON clauses.
brief.thread_state: Ilia Evdokimov says 0001 looks good after random-query testing found no wrong results; Solaimurugan V also tested earlier versions. Open: Ilia showed a large slowdown from 0002, which picks its fallback before path generation, so no cost comparison with the SubPlan is possible.
unclear: Whether 0001 alone can regress plans; message #12 shows a pulled-up plan slower than the SubPlan, and nobody answered how to avoid it.
Whether the v5 GUC still exists in v11, and its name and default.
How 0002 will choose between the LEFT JOIN fallback and the SubPlan.
No commit message or file list is given for v8 to v11.
Whether the two patches are meant to be committed together or separately.

objections.title: Moving the correlated qual to WHERE already gives the semi join
objections.failure_scenario: A user whose ON-correlated EXISTS runs well as a SubPlan upgrades, and 0001 now pulls it up into a slower plan, as in message #12 (about 70 s instead of 68 s). Users who wanted the semi join could already get it by writing the correlation in WHERE.
objections.argument: For inner joins not under an outer join's nullable side, 0001 moves the ON qual to WHERE. A user can make the same rewrite by hand today, and message #1 shows that the WHERE form already gets a Nested Loop Semi Join. The thread shows no field report, ORM output or -general thread where users write or generate the ON form and cannot change it; the only outside motivation, the Cloudberry case in message #29, is for 0002. In [P3], a pull-up of hand-written forms was rejected until real-world cases were shown.
objections.author_must_show: Which applications or query generators emit correlated EXISTS with the correlation in an inner join ON clause and cannot be changed to put it in WHERE?

objections.title: 0002 rests on one external bug discussion and slows queries that were fast
objections.failure_scenario: A user has a LEFT JOIN whose ON clause has an EXISTS that is fast today as an index-only SubPlan. After upgrade, 0002 picks the LEFT JOIN plus HashAggregate fallback before path generation. The query reads and groups the whole inner table, and the user finds out from a slower production query.
objections.argument: The only stated motivation for 0002 is a Cloudberry bug discussion (message #29), which comes from a fork, and no Postgres user report is cited. Message #30 shows a query going from about 0.2 ms to 36 ms because the rewrite is chosen without costing. The cost falls on users whose queries already run well, while the gain is for an unmeasured group. [P3] was rejected when nobody showed real cases where the pull-up wins, and the same question applies here.
objections.author_must_show: Which Postgres workloads put a correlated EXISTS in an outer join's ON clause, and how often is the fallback faster there than the SubPlan?

other_surviving.title: Patch 0002 rewrites to a de-duplicated LEFT JOIN without costing or proof
other_surviving.failure_scenario: A user has a LEFT JOIN whose ON clause holds an EXISTS that uses an index on both correlation keys. After upgrade, 0002 replaces the SubPlan with a HashAggregate over the whole inner table plus a CASE filter, and the query runs about 175 times slower (message #30). The user learns this from a slow query, and no setting turns the rewrite off.
other_surviving.argument: Message #29 says 0002 joins against distinct correlation keys and uses a CASE marker. Correctness of this de-duplication is shown only by SQLsmith runs. In [P7], a unique-ification rewrite was not pursued because the author was "unconvinced of the basic correctness of the transform", even though that rewrite competed on cost. 0002 has no cost check either: it is chosen before path generation, and message #30 asks how to choose with no answer yet. Ilia's random-query check in message #26 covered v8, which had only 0001.
other_surviving.author_must_show: What argument shows the distinct-key LEFT JOIN with CASE gives the same rows as the SubPlan, and how will 0002 avoid the regression shown in message #30?

other_surviving.title: 0002 replaces working SubPlan plans with an uncosted fallback
other_surviving.failure_scenario: A user has a LEFT JOIN whose ON clause holds an EXISTS that correlates to both join inputs. Today it runs as a SubPlan that does one index-only search. After upgrade, 0002 turns it into a HashAggregate over the whole inner table, and the user sees the query get much slower in production.
other_surviving.argument: Message #30 shows this case: 0.2 ms with the SubPlan against 36 ms with the fallback. 0002 chooses the fallback before path generation, so the planner cannot fall back to the SubPlan on cost, and message #30 asks how to choose. The only way to get the old plan back is to add OFFSET 0 to the query. Existing EXISTS pull-ups do not change plans for queries written this way today, so this is a new behaviour change for existing queries.
other_surviving.author_must_show: How will 0002 keep the SubPlan available when it is cheaper, so that existing outer-join ON EXISTS queries cannot get slower after upgrade?

critic.reasoning: Message #30 measures the slowdown and states that the fallback is chosen before path generation. The thread has no reply to it, and OFFSET 0 is the only shown way to keep the SubPlan.

refuted.title: 0002 picks the LEFT JOIN fallback before costing, with no way back
refuted.failure_scenario: A user has an outer join whose ON clause holds an EXISTS with a good two-column index, which runs today as a cheap SubPlan. After upgrade, 0002 always rewrites it into a grouped LEFT JOIN with a CASE join filter. The query becomes far slower, and the only workaround is adding OFFSET 0 to the query.
refuted.argument: Message #30 shows 36.6 ms with the fallback against 0.2 ms with the SubPlan, because all 100000 rows are grouped and 99999 are rejected by the CASE filter. The rewrite happens in pull_up_sublinks, before path generation, so the SubPlan never competes on cost. Fixing this needs either a costed alternative path or a different place in the planner, which is a different design. The motivation in message #29 is a bug in one fork, and the thread shows no Postgres user report for this query shape.
refuted.author_must_show: How will 0002 compare the LEFT JOIN fallback with the SubPlan on cost, and which Postgres users hit this query shape today?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-1 for the uncosted fallback and of demand-1 for the missing user reports. A new version of 0002 could solve this, and 0001 does not depend on it, so it would not be fatal.

refuted.title: No committer who knows sublink pull-up has engaged in two years
refuted.failure_scenario: The patch is committed. A later release adds an outer-join or lateral change in prepjointree.c or subselect.c, and the new walker misreads the nullable side. Users then get wrong EXISTS results with no error, and only someone who knows this code can find the cause.
refuted.argument: The rules for nullable sides here are subtle. v7 returned wrong results with outer joins (message #25), and the reviewer in message #19 found a regression-test plan change caused by a bug. Over 30 messages, the reviews come from testers and non-committers (messages #26, #30), and no committer has commented. Random-query testing lowers the risk but does not show who will own the transform after it is committed.
refuted.author_must_show: Which committer familiar with pull_up_sublinks has reviewed the nullable-side rules of 0001, and do they agree with them?

critic.reasoning: The scenario is a possible future bug from an unnamed later change, and the v7 wrong results were fixed in v8 and then tested in message #26. That no committer has commented is true, but it belongs in the committability field.

refuted.title: Bundling 0002 with 0001 ties a reviewed change to an unresolved one
refuted.failure_scenario: A committer who is ready to push 0001 has to decide whether the shared subquery preparation is shaped for 0002. If it is, 0001 carries hooks for a fallback that may never be accepted, and later code has to keep that shape.
refuted.argument: Message #29 says 0002 shares subquery preparation with the existing semijoin and antijoin conversion. Message #30 approves 0001 and leaves the 0002 strategy open. The material does not say whether 0001 stands alone or was changed to prepare for 0002.
refuted.author_must_show: Can 0001 be committed alone without any code that exists only to serve 0002?

critic.reasoning: 0001 was posted alone as v8 to v10 and reviewed in that form, and message #30 approves v11-0001 separately. Message #29 places the shared preparation in the second patch, so the series is infrastructure first and separately applicable.

refuted.title: No field evidence for 0001, and the WHERE rewrite already works
refuted.failure_scenario: A committer takes on a large new pull-up path in subselect.c that needed eleven versions to fix wrong results. The only users who gain write the correlation in an inner join's ON clause, and they could move it to WHERE today. If no real workload uses this form, the project carries the maintenance and plan-change risk for little gain.
refuted.argument: Message #1 starts from a test case the author built, and the later testers (messages #13, #21, #26) checked correctness only. Nobody reports a slow production query or ORM-generated SQL with this shape. Writing the qual in WHERE gives the semi join on master (message #1). Message #12 also shows a case where the pull-up is slower, so the patch will change some plans for the worse.
refuted.author_must_show: Which applications or ORMs generate correlated quals in inner join ON clauses inside EXISTS, and what speedups did their users see?

precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets the planner pull up an ANY sublink whose subquery references the immediate outer query level (varlevelsup = 1) by rewriting it as an EXISTS sublink. Today convert_ANY_sublink_to_join gives up on such sublinks, so they run as SubPlans.

Richard Guo showed that without a limit on outer references, LATERAL constraints can leave no legal join order ("failed to build any 3-way joins"). The v2 patch then stopped applying on HEAD, nobody posted a rebased version, and the entry was returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Consider parallel for LATERAL subqueries having LIMIT/OFFSET
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes set_rel_consider_parallel so that a lateral subquery with LIMIT/OFFSET may still be considered for parallel query, so a Gather can go above the whole nested loop. A later version allows this only when rel->lateral_relids is not empty.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author argued that each outer row gets its own execution of the limited subquery, but Tom Lane (seen only in quoted text) and Robert Haas were not convinced this is safe. Tom Lane noted that the patch took any lateral dependency as enough, even one that does not feed the limited subquery. Robert Haas said the real issue is where parameters are set and used, which the LATERAL keyword does not capture. The commitfest manager returned it because no further review was coming, and asked for a more rigorous correctness argument or simpler constraints.

precedents_retrieved.title: Parallelize correlated subqueries that execute within each worker
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets the planner build parallel plans for queries with correlated subplans when each subplan runs entirely within one parallel worker, so no Param value has to pass between workers. After review, the design changed to treat PARAM_EXEC params as parallel safe by default, track required params on each rel, and insert a Gather node only where that set is empty.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The thread shows no author reply after Tomas Vondra's July 2024 review, and the entry was returned with feedback in October 2024. That review found that regression tests failed on a changed plan in select_parallel, reported a compiler warning, and listed code comments. It also said no reviewer was able to confirm that the PARAM handling is correct.

precedents_retrieved.title: Convert NOT IN to anti-joins when possible
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes the planner convert a NOT IN subquery into an anti-join when it can prove that neither the subquery output nor the outer expression can be NULL. The planner would do this without costing, as it already does for NOT EXISTS.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Antonin Houska showed that join quals used as not-null proofs can be wrong when the NOT IN is in a JOIN/ON clause, because join order may let NULLs reach the anti-join. David Rowley limited the optimisation to WHERE-clause quals, and Antonin then sent review comments on that version. The author said he had no time to respond, and the entry was returned with feedback after about three months with no update.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
It has been close to three months since this last update, so marked
the patch as returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Convert join OR clauses into UNION queries
precedents_retrieved.summary: The planner would rewrite a query whose WHERE clause has an OR with arms that each reference a different joined relation into a UNION with one arm per relation. It removes duplicate rows by sort/unique on the CTIDs of the base relations, and it builds this as an extra path that competes on cost with the normal plan.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane, the patch author, said he was still not convinced that the unique-ification step is correct, and he would not work on it further without a proof. Noah Misch's review, with assertion failures and a case where planning was 170 times slower and the chosen plan 4.5 times slower, got no reply for a month, so the entry was returned with feedback.

correctness of the transform (specifically the unique-ification approach).

precedents_retrieved.title: CREATE ROLE IF NOT EXISTS
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds CREATE ROLE IF NOT EXISTS (and the same for USER and GROUP), which checks only whether the role exists and validates nothing else. A later version changed it to CREATE OR REPLACE ROLE, which passes the command to AlterRole when the role already exists.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers objected that silently reusing or redefining an existing role is risky. Their example: a role that another user created and granted to others could be made SUPERUSER by mistake, and nothing records who owns a role. Stephen Frost supported the feature with ownership checks. The entry was then left Waiting on Author after a January 2022 review, and the visible messages show no later reply from the author.

amount of relations with a portion of them being heavily updated, this
could cause autovacuum to lock down, with autovacuum workers attempting
repeatedly those jobs on the same relations for the same database, that
just kept being skipped.  This lock down can be solved with a manual
VACUUM FREEZE.

Justin King has reported one environment where the issue happened, and
Julien Rouhaud and I have been able to reproduce it in a second
environment.  With a very aggressive autovacuum_freeze_max_age,
triggering those jobs with pgbench is a matter of minutes, and hitting
the lock down is a lot harder (my local tests failed to do that).

Note that anti-wraparound and non-aggressive jobs can only be triggered
on a subset of shared catalogs:
- pg_auth_members
- pg_authid
- pg_database
- pg_replication_origin
- pg_shseclabel
- pg_subscription
- pg_tablespace
While the lock down was possible down to v12, the root cause of those
jobs is a much older issue, which needs more analysis.

Bonus thanks to Andres Freund for the discussion.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent matches 0001. It applies the existing non-costed WHERE-clause semi join conversion to ON clauses, and reviewers in messages #26 and #30 report it correct. The one objection concerns 0002 only.

0001 makes ON-clause correlation behave like WHERE-clause correlation, which the planner already pulls up without costing. The slower plan in message #12 follows that existing practice, so I raise no objection to 0001. I could not check whether the v5 GUC still exists in v11.

The proposal changes only planner rewriting of EXISTS sublinks. It adds no on-disk format, WAL record, catalog column, wire protocol message or replication behaviour. A possible GUC from v5 touches no persistent state. Standbys and subscribers do not see plan choices. Plans do not cross nodes, so no extension ABI concern is visible from the material.

The proposal has no privilege or exposure aspect. Both patches change only how the planner turns EXISTS sublinks the user already wrote into semi, anti or left joins, so no new privilege, role, function or visible data is involved. Qual ordering against RLS and security barrier quals uses the same security_level handling as today's WHERE-correlated pull-up. Without the code, I could not check that moved ON-clause quals keep that handling.
0001 alone copies the existing uncosted EXISTS pull-up for WHERE-clause correlation. So the regression in message #12 is existing behavior and is not raised here. The v5 GUC could not be checked.
0002 has no simple user rewrite in the material, so this angle raises nothing against it.
Two objections are raised. Both ask for evidence of demand and are not rejections of the idea.
